But the forward P/E read is less alarming: ~19x is actually a touch below its own 5-year average, so the extreme Buffett reading is being driven more by margin/earnings mix (and companies' overseas revenue inflating cap vs. domestic GDP) than by a classic multiple blow-off.

📚 Today you learned

Estimated vs. Confirmed Earnings Dates

Today's large-cap radar needed TSLA and MSFT dates, and both only exist as analyst/aggregator "estimated" dates (~Oct 28), extrapolated from last year's reporting calendar — neither company has issued an official press release confirming it yet. Same story for GOOG's own earnings, sitting in your position notes as just "late Oct." Companies typically confirm the exact date and time 2-3 weeks out via an 8-K or IR press release. Trading the estimated date as if it were locked is a real trap: if the actual date slips a few days, a pre-earnings trim/hold decision you timed off the wrong date fires on the wrong session. Check the company's own IR page once you're inside 2 weeks, not an aggregator.

Also today: GF Score / quant overvaluation screens — one quant model (GuruFocus) flags GOOG "Significantly Overvalued" off its GF Value, even though its PEG-style read elsewhere looks reasonable. Different valuation frameworks weighting different inputs can disagree sharply on the exact same stock at the exact same price — no single screen is the final word.
